hints: Find the driving force from power using $P = F_D \cdot v$ with $P = 75\text{ kW} = 75000\text{ W}$ and $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction: $F_{\text{net}} = F_D - R = ma$.
walkthrough:
Determine the forward driving force $F_D$ produced by the engine from the given power:
$$P = F_D \cdot v \implies F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{75000}{25} = 3000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally, where the net force is the driving force minus the resistance force:
$$F_D - R = ma \implies 3000 - 1350 = 1200a$$

Solve the equation for acceleration $a$:
$$1650 = 1200a \implies a = \frac{1650}{1200} = \frac{11}{8} = 1.375\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Start with the power formula relating driving force $F_D$ and velocity $v$:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Rearrange to solve for the driving force $F_D$ by dividing both sides by $v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute the power $P = 75\text{ kW} = 75000\text{ W}$ and speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{75000}{25} = 3000\text{ N}$$

Calculate the net forward force by subtracting the backward resistance of $1350\text{ N}$ from the forward driving force:
$$F_{\text{net}} = F_D - R = 3000 - 1350 = 1650\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = m \times a$) and substitute mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$:
$$1650 = 1200 \times a$$

Divide both sides by $1200$ to isolate acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{1650}{1200} = \frac{11}{8} = 1.375\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: At constant speed up the slope, the acceleration is zero, so driving force balances both the resistance and the component of weight down the slope: $F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$.
Use $\sin\theta = 0.1$, $m = 1200\text{ kg}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to evaluate $F_D$.
Use $v = \frac{P}{F_D}$ with $P = 76.5\text{ kW} = 76500\text{ W}$ to find the constant speed.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane. Because the car moves at constant speed, the net force is zero ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0 \implies F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$$

Substitute the given values $R = 1350\text{ N}$, $m = 1200\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\theta = 0.1$:
$$F_D = 1350 + 1200(10)(0.1) = 1350 + 1200 = 2550\text{ N}$$

Use the power formula $P = F_D \cdot v$ to solve for the constant speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{P}{F_D} = \frac{76500}{2550} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Because the car travels up the incline at constant speed, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the forward driving force must exactly balance all forces pulling backwards down the slope:
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$$

Calculate the backward weight component pulling down the hill using $m = 1200\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\theta = 0.1$:
$$mg\sin\theta = 1200 \times 10 \times 0.1 = 1200\text{ N}$$

Add the resistance force ($1350\text{ N}$) and the weight component to find the required driving force:
$$F_D = 1350 + 1200 = 2550\text{ N}$$

Start with the power equation $P = F_D \times v$ and rearrange to solve for speed $v$ by dividing both sides by $F_D$:
$$v = \frac{P}{F_D}$$

Substitute the new power $P = 76.5\text{ kW} = 76500\text{ W}$ and $F_D = 2550\text{ N}$:
$$v = \frac{76500}{2550} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
